assumptions: Operator established in Poland (pricing in PLN); adult learners (18+); consumers and professional buyers; EU and international sales; AI via third-party providers (planned, Phase 4); payments via Stripe (planned, Stage 7); hosting on Vercel and Supabase (planned). To be confirmed by the Academy.

items.requirement: Lawful basis identified and documented for every processing purpose
items.evidence: Draft Privacy Policy lists purposes and bases; consent records for recording and marketing (consents table, E2E tested)
items.gaps: Bases not validated by a specialist; records of processing not written
items.owner: Data controller (Academy Owner) with DPO/privacy adviser
items.action: Validate bases; complete Record of Processing Activities

items.requirement: Record of Processing Activities (RoPA)
items.applies: Yes — processing is not occasional, so the under-250-employees exemption does not apply
items.evidence: Draft RoPA with 9 processing activities: docs/policies/RECORD_OF_PROCESSING.md
items.gaps: Controller identity missing; legal bases and transfers not validated by a specialist
items.action: Specialist review; complete controller details; keep up to date

items.requirement: Transparent privacy information to learners
items.evidence: /privacy (draft) updated 27 Nov 2026 to describe current processing accurately: no recordings or AI active, workshop logs, MFA, hashed rate-limit keys, complete export
items.gaps: Legal entity, contact, retention periods and processor list are placeholders; not legally reviewed
items.action: Complete placeholders; legal review; publish version history

items.requirement: Data subject rights: access, portability, erasure, rectification, objection
items.evidence: Self-service export now covers every table holding learner data (profile, roles, consents, deletion requests, enrolments, progress, quizzes, Final Tasks, workshop logs, instructor assessments, MFA factors); automated test checks every table with a user_id column is exported and no other learner's data is included (tests/e2e/priority1.cjs); deletion request (E2E)
items.gaps: No staff workflow or deadline tracking for completing deletion and access requests
items.action: Extend export to all learner data; build request-handling workflow with one-month response deadline

items.requirement: Data Protection Impact Assessment before processing recordings and AI-generated feedback
items.source: GDPR Art. 35; UODO list of processing operations requiring a DPIA
items.applies: Likely yes — innovative technology, evaluation of individuals, voice and video
items.gaps: No DPIA
items.action: Carry out a DPIA before Phase 4 goes live

items.requirement: Data processing agreements with all processors
items.applies: Yes (Supabase, Vercel, email provider, AI provider, analytics; Stripe partly as an independent controller)
items.evidence: Processor register drafted: docs/policies/PROCESSOR_REGISTER.md
items.gaps: No provider contracted; DPAs not yet accepted
items.action: Accept and file each provider's DPA; keep a processor register

items.requirement: International transfer safeguards
items.applies: Yes if US providers are used (AI, hosting, email)
items.evidence: Privacy Policy draft mentions SCCs
items.gaps: Transfer mechanisms per provider not documented (EU–US Data Privacy Framework certification or SCCs; transfer impact assessment)
items.action: Document the mechanism for each provider; choose EU data regions where available

items.requirement: Retention periods defined and enforced
items.evidence: Retention Schedule proposal: docs/policies/DATA_RETENTION_SCHEDULE.md; rate-limit counters deleted automatically after 2 days
items.gaps: Periods not approved; scheduled deletion jobs not implemented
items.action: Adopt a Data Retention Schedule; implement scheduled deletion (recordings, inactive accounts, logs)

items.requirement: Personal data breach notification (72 hours to the authority; affected individuals when high risk)
items.evidence: Incident and Data Breach Response Procedure drafted: docs/operations/INCIDENT_RESPONSE.md (72-hour UODO notification, learner notification, register fields)
items.gaps: Contacts, breach register and tabletop exercise outstanding; specialist review
items.action: Adopt an Incident and Data Breach Response Procedure and a breach register

items.requirement: Data protection by design and by default
items.evidence: RLS on all 17 tables; per-user filtering of every learner query (fixes staff seeing others' rows in learner views); staff privileges require MFA; minimisation; consents off by default; hashed rate-limit keys
items.gaps: Teaching staff can read all learners' progress (not only assigned cohorts); no retention automation
items.action: Restrict staff access to assigned cohorts; implement retention

items.requirement: No solely automated decisions with legal or similarly significant effects
items.evidence: No AI or automated assessment exists; Competent can only be set by a human assessor (database function, tested); certificate requires human approval
items.gaps: Must be maintained when AI feedback is introduced in Phase 4
items.action: Keep AI output advisory; re-verify in the Phase 4 audit

items.requirement: Data Protection Officer appointment (or documented decision not to appoint)
items.applies: Probably not mandatory (no large-scale special-category processing or large-scale systematic monitoring), but the decision must be documented
items.gaps: No documented DPO decision
items.action: Document the decision; consider an external privacy adviser

items.requirement: Special-category data not processed unnecessarily (health, biometrics)
items.evidence: No health fields collected; recordings are not used for identification (therefore not biometric data in the GDPR sense); Terms and FAQ prohibit patient data
items.gaps: Learners may disclose their own health information (e.g. anxiety, stammering) in free text; no guidance at input points
items.action: Add guidance at free-text inputs; never use voice for identification

items.requirement: No patient-identifiable or confidential clinical data in learner submissions
items.type: Legally mandatory (for learners as data controllers of patient data) / platform safeguard
items.evidence: Warnings in Terms, Privacy Policy, FAQ, contact form, every exercise and the W1 Briefing ("Record only yourself"); recordings never uploaded; fictional examples
items.gaps: No technical detection; no process for removing content that is reported
items.action: Add a reporting and removal procedure; consider a warning at submission

items.requirement: Adult learners only; age confirmation
items.applies: Yes (programme is for qualified and training doctors)
items.evidence: Sign-up requires acceptance of the Terms (required checkbox), and the Terms draft states that users must be at least 18
items.gaps: No explicit age or professional-status confirmation; Terms not reviewed
items.action: Add explicit age confirmation at sign-up and checkout

items.requirement: Prohibition of emotion recognition in education (AI must not infer learners' emotions)
items.source: EU AI Act Art. 5(1)(f); applicable since 2 Feb 2025
items.evidence: Code review 26 Nov 2026: no AI, camera or voice analysis exists in the platform; approved design limits feedback to observable communication behaviours; requirement written into AI governance requirements (AUDIT_REPORT §3)
items.gaps: Must be enforced in AI prompts, features and vendor selection (no 'nervousness' or 'confidence' detection from face or voice)
items.action: Include in Phase 4 acceptance criteria and test cases

items.requirement: Classification of AI feedback: high-risk if used to evaluate learning outcomes or steer the learning process
items.source: EU AI Act Art. 6 and Annex III point 3; Art. 6(3) derogation
items.applies: To be confirmed — depends on whether AI output influences completion, assessment or certification
items.evidence: Design keeps AI feedback formative and advisory; human assessor decides outcomes
items.gaps: No documented classification; dates of high-risk obligations to be verified (possible postponement under EU 'digital omnibus' proposals)
items.action: Formal classification before Phase 4; if high-risk, implement Chapter III obligations or redesign

items.requirement: Transparency: learners informed they interact with an AI system; AI-generated audio/text identifiable
items.applies: Yes once AI teachers and simulations are live
items.evidence: Public pages state AI teachers are software and can make mistakes
items.gaps: In-product disclosure, AI labelling of generated voices and feedback not yet built (Phase 4)
items.action: Build disclosure into every AI interaction; label AI-generated audio

items.requirement: AI literacy of staff who operate or oversee AI systems
items.source: EU AI Act Art. 4; applicable since 2 Feb 2025
items.applies: Yes once AI is deployed; prudent now
items.gaps: No AI literacy training record for instructors and assessors
items.action: Create a short AI literacy module for staff; keep training records

items.requirement: No use of learner recordings or conversations for model training without a valid basis and consent
items.evidence: Privacy Policy and Responsible AI Policy state no training on learner data; processor register requires contractual exclusion
items.gaps: Provider settings (training opt-out, retention) not configured or documented
items.action: Choose providers and settings that exclude training; document in the processor register

items.requirement: Human oversight and transparent limitations of AI feedback
items.source: EU AI Act Art. 14 (if high-risk); GDPR Art. 22; approved Academy rule
items.evidence: Responsible AI Policy drafted (docs/policies/RESPONSIBLE_AI_POLICY.md); assessment statuses set only by humans with MFA (implemented and tested)
items.gaps: Not implemented in product
items.action: Implement human review points and a limitation notice with every AI report

items.requirement: Consent before non-essential cookies or similar technologies

items.requirement: Prior consent for marketing emails; easy withdrawal

items.requirement: HTTP security headers (CSP, HSTS, frame-ancestors, nosniff, Referrer-Policy, Permissions-Policy); framework banner removed

items.gaps: Production Auth rate-limit settings to be verified when hosted project is created

items.requirement: Multi-factor authentication for staff accounts with access to learner data

items.requirement: Secure storage of learner recordings and files (private buckets, signed URLs, size and type limits, retention)

items.gaps: Design required before Phase 4
items.action: Private bucket with per-user RLS, short-lived signed URLs, malware and type checks, automated deletion
